text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past category, genre, or device-family interactions as broad continuing demand for related items.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations connect when they support a concrete task established by repeated purchases, such as measuring hardware, repairing connections, or expanding compatible storage.",
    "Entertainment choices connect when they preserve the specific mood, musical intensity, or story qualities users value in recent selections."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad associations repeatedly substitute for demonstrated needs, turning repair shopping into assumed demand for printing supplies and accessory purchases into demand for entertainment devices.",
    "Familiar product families produce redundant or older-device recommendations without evidence of an upgrade, replacement, or additional capability being needed.",
    "Broad entertainment similarities overlook distinctions that determine choice, including comedy versus drama, gentle vocals versus heavy guitars, and familiar compilations versus exploratory albums."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, brand, or broad genre is repeatedly treated as sufficient evidence of relevance.",
    "Widely familiar items and multiple variants of the same product type recur despite weak support for their underlying purpose."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent and repeated interactions provide specific evidence of current tasks, listening occasions, moods, and desired intensity that is insufficiently reflected in recommendations.",
    "Compatibility, equipment ownership, and already-satisfied needs determine whether a related accessory or device adds practical value.",
    "Unidentified items leave relevance uncertain; skips in these cases provide weak evidence of a negative content preference."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top recommendations repeatedly share broad associations with history while lacking the specific purpose, compatibility, or experiential match needed to make them worth choosing now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top recommendations users would choose for a concrete reason supported by recent or repeated interactions.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to unsupported activities, incompatible requirements, redundant ownership, or mismatched mood and intensity.",
    "The concentration of top recommendations in a product family or broad genre that users report does not meet their current needs.",
    "The frequency of uncertain relevance judgments caused by unidentified items, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
}
